title: Walled node hardening intake - OmniHealth Systems
summary: Intro discovery to map requirements for a strictly walled (no egress) private deployment. Customer has existing rack-level GPU assets, strict quarterly patch windows, and signed firmware policy. Key topics: offline update process, signed bundles, KMS/HSM constraints, model-size/quantization tradeoffs for VRAM-limited cards, and acceptance testing/benchmarking. Agreed next steps: share security pack, run onsite hardware audit, and schedule a 2-week pilot with a 2-node cluster in their lab environment.
topics: Offline update signing and firmware policy
Hardware constraints: GPU memory and thermals
next_steps: Alex Moreno: Send Redwood Private security pack + SOC2/ISO artifacts (by 2027-02-12)
Priya Shah: Schedule 1.5-hour lab hardware scan and benchmark day (target week of 2027-02-22)
OmniHealth (Marcus): Provide rack HW inventory + BIOS/firmware baseline (by 2027-02-15)
action_items: Alex (AE): Share network diagram template and example private-control-plane topology - due 2027-02-12
Priya (SE): Draft pilot plan (2-node, 4-GPU per node) and required test harness - due 2027-02-16
Marcus (Infra): Export GPU inventory and current driver/firmware versions - due 2027-02-15
Jenna (InfoSec): List approved HSM vendors and airgap acceptance criteria - due 2027-02-18
transcript:
Meeting header
09:22 PST — 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ramos (CTO, OmniHealth), Jenna Holt (Head InfoSec), Marcus Li (Infra Lead), Samir Bhatt (Regulatory)

Summary: quick intro and then deep into offline update mechanics, HW mapping, and acceptance tests.

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, Alex from Redwood - thanks for carving out time. we'll keep this focused, want to understand the walled environment constraints.
00:18 Dr. Elena: Hi, thanks. We run patient-facing inference in our own colo and cannot allow outbound calls to public control planes. basically airwalled.
00:28 Jenna: Right, and compliance needs signed updates only. no USB, no manual installs unless checksums signed by our HSM.
00:40 Priya: Okay, that's helpful. Our Redwood Private supports a private control plane pattern; there are offline bundle workflows where we produce signed update artifacts you can verify with your KMS. How are you currently doing signed firmware or software rollouts?
01:02 Marcus: Today we use vendor-signed firmware and an internal tool that validates signatures against our HSM. patch windows are quarterly; emergency patches are very gated. Also some of our older racks have A10s and older Ampere 80GB cards but a few nodes are 32GB A100s only.
01:27 Alex: Good — so we need to consider models and memory footprint. for nodes with 32GB VRAM we might want int8 quant or smaller model variants. Priya, can you walk through the offline bundle process?
01:40 Priya: Sure. High level: we build a deploy bundle that contains the runtime, model artifacts (optional delta for model weights), and orchestration metadata. the bundle can be signed by Redwood and then re-signed or re-keyed by your HSM for final acceptance. Bundle verification runs at install time and the node refuses to apply anything not signed by your key.
02:05 Jenna: That fits our policy. question: does bundle verification require any outbound key check? we can't allow any egress.
02:14 Priya: No — verification is local. the node has a verification agent that validates the signature chain and checks certificate revocation lists that you can provide as part of the offline package. we also support a policy where you mlock the key material into an HSM and only import transient verification keys for the upgrade window.
02:35 Samir: And for audit — do you provide install-time provenance logs? we need tamper-evident records for regulators.
02:42 Priya: yes, we emit audit logs that can be written to an append-only store. we can format them to meet your retention window and include the signed bundle hash, installer identity, and step-by-step exit codes. If you prefer, we can route logs to an on-prem SIEM via a push during your maintenance window.
03:03 Dr. Elena: On the model side, we have two main workloads: clinical summarization (batch, large contexts) and real-time triage (low-latency, single-request). Triage needs <150ms p99 ideally but we know tradeoffs.
03:20 Alex: For p99 in a walled setup you'll likely choose Dedicated-like reserved capacity but private. With limited VRAM older cards, batching and quantization will be the main levers. Priya — thoughts on caching?
03:33 Priya: We have prefix/KV caching and continuous batching in the runtime. On small cards, we recommend offloading KV cache to NVMe-backed local cache or use model sharding so the hot KV is resident. also reduce context window if possible for triage.
03:50 Marcus: NVMe cache is OK. we can't do model sharding across nodes due to our network isolation?
03:58 Priya: Node-local sharding is possible; cross-node inference requires network and we avoid that for airgapped. we'll size models per node.
04:10 Jenna: What about key management? our policy mandates HSM for any master keys and we cannot have Redwood hold keys.
04:17 Alex: That's supported. Redwood Private can be configured to use customer-managed KMS/HSM; only signed tokens are used by the runtime and we never persist plaintext keys in our control plane. In fully offline cases the control plane runs behind your VPC or on a physically separated manager that you operate.
04:36 Samir: Any certification matrix? we need to know what parts of your stack are SOC2 and what components are simply engineering controls.
04:45 Alex: We'll provide a security pack with SOC2 Type II, ISO artifacts, pen test summaries, and a private deployment checklist that indicates which responsibilities remain with OmniHealth vs Redwood.
04:58 Marcus: Thermal and power are concerns. Some of our racks are older; can you advise on operational overhead for continuous inference?
05:07 Priya: We'll bring a sizing guide. For steady low-latency triage at p99 150ms, with 32GB cards you might only manage smaller models like 7B quantized. For large-context summarization we recommend dedicated 80GB nodes or burst policies to a different cluster. If 80GB aren't available, we can run summarization as batch jobs overnight.
05:29 Dr. Elena: Sounds pragmatic. What about rollback? if a bundle causes regressions we need a fast path to revert.
05:37 Priya: Bundles are versioned and we keep the previous install on node until a successful health-check window completes. rollback is a local operation that doesn't require egress; the orchestration can be triggered by a local operator or via Redwood's private control plane if you enable it.
05:57 Jenna: For acceptance test, what metrics do you recommend we capture during pilot?
06:02 Priya: Latency p50/p95/p99, token cost, model output tokenization diffs vs baseline, memory pressure, and cold-start times. We'll provide the test harness to replay a canonical set of prompts.
06:18 Marcus: We'll need CPU/IO numbers too since NVMe caching will hit drives.
06:22 Priya: Absolutely. the harness captures IO and CPU counters.
06:27 Alex: Okay, near-term next steps: I'll send the security artifacts and network diagram template. Priya will draft the pilot plan and test harness. Marcus will share HW inventory.
06:36 Dr. Elena: Target pilot window late Feb is good. Also, can you provide rough pricing for a 2-node pilot and for ongoing support?
06:45 Alex: We'll include a pilot quote and options for annual reserved pricing if you need dedicated capacity. We'll also include a line for professional services to run the initial on-site install.
06:55 Jenna: One more item — our compliance team insists on signed firmware images for GPUs. do you coordinate firmware upgrades?
07:02 Priya: We don't push vendor firmware; we provide orchestration hooks. you retain final control and must apply vendor-signed firmware. our installer honors firmware baselines and will refuse to run if firmware deviates from approved list.
07:18 Dr. Elena: Great. that's it from us. thanks.
07:22 Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites for the lab day.
07:28 Meeting end.

Notes: transcription contains speaker turns and occasional mis-recognitions (Speaker 6 label used). Some technical terms have been simplified in transcript (e.g., K-V cash vs KV cache).
